transcript.text: theres water in the bottom of my frige under the salad draws, keeps comming back after i mop it up

Water pooling under the salad drawers that keeps returning is almost always caused by a blocked defrost drain. When the fridge cycles, frost melts into water that should run down this hole to an evaporation tray at the back of the appliance; if it's clogged, the water backs up and spills onto the shelves. Please check the bottom rear wall inside the fridge for a small drain hole or channel. Is it visible, and does it look blocked by debris or ice?

yes theres a little groove and a hole at the bottom of the back wall, its got bits of lettuce and gunk in it. also sometimes theres droplets and a bit of ice on the back wall and water runs down. the water is only inside the fridge not near the plug or on the floor outside

[Heading: Likely cause: drain hose]
That suggests it: the drain hole was blocked by debris, which caused the water to back up into the base. To help me check if there are any specific recalls or known issues for your appliance, could you please tell me the make and model number? It's usually on a sticker inside the fridge, often on a side wall near the salad drawers.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its a Beko, the model on the sticker inside the fridge says CFG1582W. what should i do about the gunk in the hole, can i clear it myself?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain hose]
Yes, you can clear it yourself safely. First, unplug the fridge to be safe. Use a turkey baster or a small squeezy bottle filled with warm (not boiling) water to flush out the lettuce and gunk from that hole at the bottom of the back wall; place a towel underneath to catch the runoff. If the water doesn't flow freely, you can gently use a flexible pipe cleaner or a piece of soft wire to dislodge any remaining blockage deeper in the tube. Once it's clear, pour another jug of warm water through to confirm it drains away quickly into the evaporation tray at the back of the appliance. If the water still pools after this, there may be a more serious internal issue requiring an engineer.

ok i done it with a cotton bud and some warm water, got all the lettuce and gunk out and the water went straight down the hole. its been a few days now and no more water pooling in the bottom, seems sorted

[Heading: Likely cause: drain hose]
That is excellent news. To help prevent it from happening again, try to keep food items a little way off the back wall so they don't trap debris against the drain hole, and avoid putting very hot food directly inside without covering it. If you notice any water building up again in the future, just give us a call.
